title: The Render Slate — delivery wrapper for every executable prompt
completeTableMarkdown:
| Row | Content |
|---|---|
| `Render ID` | `<PROJECT>_<Shot ID>__<platform-model>__<operation>__P<nn>` (ID discipline below) |
| `Intent` | One director-readable line: shot, action, decisive creative constraint; opens with `Canon: DRAFT — approve the treatment before running` when the treatment is not yet approved (rule 14) |
| `Crew choices` | Two halves. *Left to the model:* the axes this prompt deliberately does not instruct. *Decided by the crew:* the craft-fillable decisions the canon did not fix, every look control included — the director's veto list (rule 14). Example: `Left to the model: composition inside the shot sizes, cut timing, body mechanics, wet fur and brass, the light bloom. Decided by the crew: medium-wide → close-up → medium-wide; one camera line, low at the cat's shoulder height, looking toward the lever; the rain shake as the reaction cue.` |
| `Run in` | The RECEIPT chain platform → access route → project/workspace → surface/tool → model → mode as `id ("UI label")`, then the KEY and its receipt state (rule 17). Example: `Higgsfield → web UI → project LIGHTCAT → Video → Seedance 2.5 → t2v (UI label unverified — read the live task dropdown) — from reference HF-WEB@2026-09-04, not live-checked this session; confirm model, mode and workspace on the live form before Generate` |
| `Settings` | Executable UI values: ratio, resolution, duration, audio, any non-default control. Never repeat a UI setting inside a video prompt — no double control (exceptions: the take's duration where the technique's form carries it; a control the project's A/B proved inert, platform-ui-workflows §1; the Higgsfield DoP tool, production-pipeline ch. 16). Still prompts keep the canvas/aspect/grid line in the prompt, first, AND set it in the UI (style-control §2) |
| `Lint` | Every video prompt, in any technique: `words n · negations n/1 · numerals outside TC n/0 · absolute measures n/0 · double mentions none · contradictions none · beats complete` (definitions and counting rules: ch. 12h; `words` is a count for the rule-15 ratchet, never a ceiling; each numeral exception is a look control named in Crew choices) |
| `Inputs` | One line per reference, numbered in slot/upload order: `n. @tag = what it is — its one job`; say whether the anchor is a reference or a literal start/end frame (rule 1); on a platform with a persistent library say "Elements, no upload"; add `🟡 token form unverified — match the upload label before running` when the surface could not be seen (ch. 12b) |

title: Selection index: brief → recipe
completeTableMarkdown:
| Project constraint | Favors | Penalizes |
|---|---|---|
| Low reroll budget / tight deadline | Malick (mosaic of short moments), Boyle (montage), Ozu (locked frontal statics), Gilligan (wordless process montage) | Tarkovsky, Lubezki-style oners — long coherent takes mean extension chains + high reroll cost |
| Complex action, crowds, physics risk | Greengrass, UGC, Lynch — absorb or legitimize artifacts; Kurosawa — telephoto crowd planes + weather cover | Fincher, Kubrick — surgical frames expose every flaw |
| Dialogue-heavy | Ozu (frontal singles sidestep reverse-angle continuity), Tarantino, Bergman | Greengrass — verité dialogue coverage burns takes |
| Film lives on face performance | Bergman + Nykvist — spend the reroll budget here | Willis (buried eyes), heavy-silhouette styles |
| High continuity risk (many locations/outfits/characters) | Malick, Lynch — elliptical/dream logic tolerates jumps | Nolan cross-cutting — parallel lines punish continuity errors |
| Stylized/animated format | Miyazaki, Anderson, Pixar → pixar-look.md | Fraser/Willis deep underexposure — clashes with readable-face warmth |

title: Harmony map: which packages combine
completeTableMarkdown:
| Director recipe | DoP signature | Why it harmonizes |
|---|---|---|
| Spielberg | Kamiński | Blown godlight + smoke gives the wonder-and-threat grammar its sentiment and its war-memory grit — both extremes in one toolkit |
| Nolan | Hoytema | Monumental sober naturalism scales to IMAX mechanisms without gloss; cool restraint matches engineered structure |
| Villeneuve | Deakins → Fraser | Deakins built the monumental-clarity phase; Fraser's texture-first underexposure carries the later dust-and-dread scale — both serve duration-dread |
| Wong Kar-wai | Doyle | Step-printed neon smear IS the longing; structure and image are inseparable here — adopt them together or not at all |
| Bergman | Nykvist | The face-as-landscape structure needs the face-light standard; nothing decorative survives the chamber |
| Allen lineage | Willis | The amber NY period — master-shot talk in underexposed warm rooms; comedy that trusts darkness |
| Sciamma | Mathon | The gaze structure needs flame-and-dusk honesty; portrait stillness is shared doctrine |
| Malick | Lubezki | Wandering whisper-montage requires a camera that lives in natural light and moves like breath |
| Wenders | Müller | Available-light Americana trust — the seeing-road structure needs a camera that treats neon and dusk as sufficient |
| Gilligan | (Michael Slovis / BCS lineage) | Hard-sun neo-western wides, object-POV wit, and time-lapse punctuation were built WITH the house camera department — the image grammar is part of the recipe; no full second package |
| Kubrick / Tarantino / Fincher / Scorsese / Ridley Scott / Wright / Wachowskis | (house signatures) | Their image grammar is baked into the director recipe itself — no external DoP package needed; adding one dilutes |

title: 2. Composition
completeTableMarkdown:
| Tool | Effect | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| Rule of thirds | Natural, balanced | Default; subject on a power point, gaze into open space |
| Central/symmetric | Formal, controlled, confrontational or comic | Authority, ritual, deadpan; breaks feel deliberate |
| Leading lines | Steers the eye | Reveals, depth, connecting subject↔goal |
| Frame-in-frame | Isolation, voyeurism, entrapment | Doorways, windows, mirrors-as-shape (not reflections) |
| Negative space | Loneliness, insignificance, dread | Small subject vs. big empty area; horror off-screen space |
| Headroom/lead room | Comfort norms | Break them (crowded headroom, no lead room) for unease |
| Depth layering | Immersion, scale | Always name FG/MG/BG (ties into location plates) |
| High vs. low horizon | Sky = fate/freedom; ground = weight/burden | Establishings, emotional wides |
| Balance/imbalance | Stability vs. tension | Tilt/dutch and asymmetry signal "something is wrong" |

title: 4. Editing
completeTableMarkdown:
| Cut | Function |
|---|---|
| Hard cut on action | Invisible continuity — cut mid-movement, the motion hides the seam |
| Match cut (graphic/motion) | Poetic linkage across space/time; scene transitions |
| Cut on look (eyeline) | Question → answer: face looks, next shot shows what they see (Kuleshov: the pairing CREATES the emotion) |
| J-cut (audio leads) | Pulls forward, smooth scene entry — sound of the next scene starts under the current one |
| L-cut (audio trails) | Reaction room — we watch listeners while the speaker continues |
| Jump cut | Time compression, nervous energy, comedy of repetition |
| Smash cut | Violent contrast (loud→silent, calm→chaos); comedy and shock |
| Cutaway/insert | Detail emphasis, tension objects, hiding continuity errors |
| Cross-cutting | Parallel action = suspense engine; alternate locations, tighten intervals toward collision |
| Ellipsis | Skip the unfilmable/boring; the audience's mind bridges (also the AI rescue tool, renderability) |
| Scene transitions | Sound bridge (audio crosses the cut — the workhorse) · match dissolve (time passing, memory) · hard black (chapter weight) · whip/wipe (playful momentum, period flavor) — pick ONE transition language per film |

title: 24f. Negation & exclusion — a channel decision, not a wording choice
completeTableMarkdown:
| Model class | Exclusion channel that works |
|---|---|
| Diffusion stills (FLUX, SD3.5, Midjourney, Imagen) | Dedicated negative field / `--no` only — bare atomic nouns ("people", "wall"), one concept per entry (compounds get split and over-exclude), NEVER "don't/no X" in the prompt body |
| AR/reasoning stills (GPT Image, Nano Banana) | Short in-prompt exclusions are vendor-endorsed ("no watermark, no extra text") and legitimate — but the positive description still carries the composition; Google's own rule: positive framing first ("empty street", not "no cars") |
| Video models | Ch. 14 negative rule governs (it's consistent with this research): Seedance takes in-prompt negations for subtitles, on-screen text and audio (official: "Use positive descriptions whenever possible. Negative constraints are supported for subtitles and audio control" [BD-off]), every other exclusion positive first; Veo/Kling use their negative fields with bare keywords, most critical first; models without a dedicated negative field → rewrite prohibitions as the desired state ("the boy waves his hands", not "can't stay still") |

title: 24g. Edits & locality
completeTableMarkdown:
| Mask type | Platforms | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **Hard** (algorithmic clamp: outside-mask content mathematically preserved) | FLUX Fill (binary b/w mask), Imagen/Vertex inpaint (`maskDilation` ~0.01) | Content cannot escape; the mask truly defines region AND size |
| **Soft** (guidance only) | GPT Image `mask` param — official: "entirely prompt-based… may not follow its exact shape"; may repaint globally (documented on the `gpt-image-2` generation; re-verify on `gpt-image-2.5` — the 2.5 edit-precision claim above may change this) | Always pair with the full prompt-level preserve list; expect overflow |
| **No pixel mask** | Nano Banana API (semantic masking by prompt only); Seedream (annotation channel: boxes/arrows/coordinates/sketch instead); Higgsfield mask-brush UI over NB Pro (rough mask OK — expand slightly when replacing, widen + regenerate when an edit misses) | Use the platform's native channel; don't assume mask semantics that aren't there |

title: 24h. Quick reference — problem → first move → hard fix
completeTableMarkdown:
| Problem | First move (prompt-level) | Hard fix (channel change) |
|---|---|---|
| Place an element | Zone language early + named scene geometry | Layout sketch → structure map/annotation → composite layers |
| Set an element's size | Object-class word + shot type/lens + ONE relational anchor | Mask drawn at size (hard-mask platform) / sketch-at-size / composite |
| Small object with detail | Detail described at target scale | Crop-zoom-inpaint-paste-back |
| Exact count | One plain number ≤4, simple background | Multi-panel / scaffolded adds / crowd sheet |
| Exclude something | Positive replacement in the same slot | Negative field (diffusion) / short exclusion (AR) / accept-and-post fallback |
| Local edit, keep the rest | "Change only X" + repeated preserve list, ≤3 iterations | Hard mask (FLUX Fill/Imagen) or restart from original with combined instruction |
| Keep composition, change content | Reference + role line ("layout and light only") | FLUX Depth/Canny structure lock |
| Layout fights you twice | Reroll seed (diffusion) or switch to AR-class model | Any of the above — but change CHANNEL, not vocabulary (24b item 7) |
| Prompt grew across runs; correct instructions stop landing | Cut back inside the model+version word budget; replace, never append (24b item 8) | Rewrite short from scratch (SKILL rule 15), then change channel |
| Only the exceptions of an object class render | Name the class's default state positively, and first (counterweight sentence, 24a) | Scaffold: generate the ordinary field, add the exceptions as an edit |
| A banned element returns right after you shortened the Avoid list | Restore it from the protected world-rule subset; cut only volatile entries (24f) | Positive replacement in the same slot instead of the ban |
| An object renders at the wrong size or distance despite a stated measure | Replace the measure with ONE relation to a named in-frame object (24d rung 3, SKILL rule 7) | Mask / box / sketch at size — numeric channel, never prose |
